HOT_DRY.name: Hot-Dry
HOT_DRY.description: Characterized by high summer ambient temperatures, intense solar radiation, low relative humidity, and large diurnal temperature swings.
HOT_DRY.source: NBC 2016 Part 11 & ECBC 2017 Guidelines for Hot-Dry Climates

layout.value: Compact courtyard house with clustered rooms and shared party walls.
layout.reason: Minimizes exposed surface-to-volume ratio to outside heat while the central courtyard induces microclimate shade and convective cool sinks.

walls.value: Thick, high thermal mass walls (adobe, rammed earth, or stone masonry).
walls.reason: Slows diurnal heat penetration with a 6-8 hour thermal lag, keeping interiors cool by day and releasing warmth during chilly desert nights.

roof.value: Insulated flat or terraced roof coated with high-albedo reflective white lime wash.
roof.reason: Bounces intense direct solar radiation away during midday while heavy insulation prevents conductive heat flow into living spaces.

windows.value: Small, deep-set punched openings oriented primarily toward the north.
windows.reason: Cuts direct glare and unwanted solar radiation entry while still admitting uniform indirect natural daylight.

shading.value: Deep external overhangs, movable louvers, and perforated jali screens.
shading.reason: Intercepts solar heat gain before it strikes glass panes and accelerates air movement through narrow vent apertures.

ventilation.value: Night-flush ventilation with tight daytime envelope closure.
ventilation.reason: Locks out scorching daytime breezes and captures cool nocturnal air currents to purge structural heat mass.

orientation.value: Long axis oriented along the East-West direction.
orientation.reason: Exposes smaller end facades to intense low-angle morning and evening sun, maximizing easily shaded north and south walls.

landscape.value: Drought-tolerant native vegetation, xeriscaping, and central water fountain or pool.
landscape.reason: Supplies localized evaporative cooling around courtyards without excessive water depletion in arid terrain.

WARM_HUMID.name: Warm-Humid
WARM_HUMID.description: Characterized by high humidity, moderate to high temperatures, heavy seasonal rainfall, and low diurnal variation.
WARM_HUMID.source: NBC 2016 Part 11 & ECBC 2017 Guidelines for Warm-Humid Climates

layout.value: Open, elongated single-banked pavilion layout with wide verandahs and stilts.
layout.reason: Maximizes cross-ventilation through every room while raised floors allow ground-level air circulation and elevate living spaces above moisture.

walls.value: Lightweight, breathable walls with timber, bamboo, or permeable louvers.
walls.reason: Retains minimal heat so the structure cools rapidly as soon as ambient evening breezes pick up.

roof.value: Steeply sloping roof with generous wide overhangs and ventilated ridges.
roof.reason: Rapidly sheds torrential monsoon rains while extensive overhangs shield perimeter walls from wind-driven downpours.

windows.value: Large shaded window openings positioned for cross-ventilation.
windows.reason: Promotes physiological cooling by maintaining continuous indoor air speed across occupants' skin.

shading.value: Continuous perimeter verandahs, fixed chhajjas, and timber lattice brise-soleil.
shading.reason: Prevents direct solar exposure on wall surfaces while allowing unrestricted airflow during humid rain showers.

ventilation.value: Continuous cross-ventilation and stack ventilation via high roof clerestories.
ventilation.reason: Dissipates trapped humid air and heat buildup through high ceiling vents.

orientation.value: Long facades facing North and South, aligned perpendicular to prevailing wind vectors.
orientation.reason: Minimizes solar radiation on side walls while catching prevailing coastal or monsoonal breezes.

landscape.value: High-canopy shade trees with cleared understory and permeable grass turf.
landscape.reason: Creates an overhead shade umbrella without blocking near-ground horizontal air circulation.

COMPOSITE.name: Composite
COMPOSITE.description: Exhibits contrasting seasonal extremes: scorching dry summers, intense monsoons, and cold winter months.
COMPOSITE.source: NBC 2016 Part 11 & ECBC 2017 Guidelines for Composite Climates

layout.value: Courtyard or semi-courtyard configuration with zoned seasonal living quarters.
layout.reason: Provides sheltered outdoor living in winter and microclimatic shade cooling throughout harsh summer months.

walls.value: Medium to high thermal mass walls (cavity brickwork or insulated fly-ash blocks).
walls.reason: Dampens severe summer daytime heat peaks while retaining indoor warmth during cold winter nights.

roof.value: Insulated concrete or vaulted roof with weatherproofing and reflective ceramic tile finish.
roof.reason: Shields against intense summer sun while heavy insulation prevents winter heat loss through the ceiling.

windows.value: Moderate window-to-wall ratio with operable double-glazed casements.
windows.reason: Can be opened fully for cross-ventilation during humid monsoons and sealed tightly against dust and winter chills.

shading.value: South overhangs sized for summer shade and winter solar ingress, with adjustable louvers.
shading.reason: Blocks high-altitude summer sun while welcoming low-altitude winter sunbeams deep into interior living rooms.

ventilation.value: Seasonal ventilation: nighttime cooling in summer, cross-drafts during monsoon, controlled air exchanges in winter.
ventilation.reason: Adapts flexibly across changing seasonal temperature and humidity regimes.

orientation.value: Longer building axis aligned East-West with primary fenestration facing South.
orientation.reason: Optimizes passive solar heating in winter while enabling easy overhang shading in summer.

landscape.value: Deciduous shade trees to the South/West and seasonal water catchments.
landscape.reason: Provides full foliage shade in summer and naturally drops leaves in winter to admit beneficial solar warming.

TEMPERATE.name: Temperate
TEMPERATE.description: Moderate ambient temperatures year-round with comfortable humidity and balanced seasonal variations.
TEMPERATE.source: NBC 2016 Part 11 & ECBC 2017 Guidelines for Temperate Climates

layout.value: Simple compact plan with integrated semi-open balconies and verandahs.
layout.reason: Promotes indoor-outdoor living while maintaining a moderate surface area for stable year-round comfort.

walls.value: Medium thermal mass walls (standard brickwork or compressed earth blocks).
walls.reason: Smooths out moderate day-to-night temperature swings without excessive insulation bulk.

roof.value: Gabled or vaulted roof with moderate slopes and rainwater harvesting gutters.
roof.reason: Handles seasonal rain effectively and facilitates natural ventilation air pockets under the ceiling.

windows.value: 20-30 percent window-to-wall area with operable double or high-performance glazing.
windows.reason: Provides ample natural daylighting and views without causing excessive heat gain or thermal leakage.

shading.value: Moderate overhangs and deciduous pergola trellises.
shading.reason: Shields direct solar glare during peak afternoon hours while allowing gentle ambient diffuse light.

ventilation.value: Cross-ventilation through opposing windows and operable ceiling vents.
ventilation.reason: Maintains continuous fresh air circulation in response to mild ambient outdoor temperatures.

orientation.value: Primary facades oriented toward North and South/Southeast.
orientation.reason: Balances natural daylighting year-round while taking advantage of prevailing gentle local breezes.

landscape.value: Evergreen and flowering perimeter shrubs, rain gardens, and permeable paving.
landscape.reason: Enhances microclimate comfort, supports local biodiversity, and absorbs seasonal storm runoff.

COLD.name: Cold
COLD.description: Characterized by sub-zero winter temperatures, snowfall or frost, high heating loads, and strong chilly winds.
COLD.source: NBC 2016 Part 11 & ECBC 2017 Guidelines for Cold Climates

layout.value: Compact, low-profile footprint with minimal perimeter envelope surface.
layout.reason: Minimizes conductive surface area exposed to freezing external temperatures and reduces total heating demand.

walls.value: Thick, heavily insulated perimeter walls (stone/rammed earth with wood or wool insulation).
walls.reason: Prevents conductive heat loss to the freezing exterior and retains internally generated living heat.

roof.value: Insulated sloped roof with snow-shedding pitch and airtight ceiling insulation.
roof.reason: Facilitates snow shedding to prevent excessive structural snow load while blocking heat loss through the roof peak.

windows.value: Large double or triple-glazed south windows with insulated shutters; minimal north windows.
windows.reason: Maximizes direct passive solar heat gain from the low southern sun while eliminating cold drafts from the north.

shading.value: Minimal permanent solar shading; retractable insulated night blinds and storm shutters.
shading.reason: Welcomes every bit of solar heat during the daytime and seals windows at night to cut radiation losses.

ventilation.value: Draught-proofing with airlocks (vestibules) and controlled heat-recovery ventilation.
ventilation.reason: Eliminates freezing cold wind infiltration while supplying essential fresh air without losing interior warmth.

orientation.value: Major glazed living facades facing true South, with service buffers to the North.
orientation.reason: Maximizes passive solar radiation capture during short winter days while northern storage rooms act as thermal buffers.

landscape.value: Dense evergreen windbreak trees planted on the North and Northwest boundaries.
landscape.reason: Deflects icy winter gales over and away from the building envelope, creating a sheltered microclimate.
